**On the historical merged main, the correction-size stop passed every affected check once two native check criteria were derived: one at its rounding floor, one as a volume accuracy target.**
The two native failures were not defects in the returned states: both pass criteria
sat at the rounding floor, and main passed them only by margin.
The action forward bound now includes the Jacobian's own evaluation error, and the
wide-ionic reference now closes its volume Newton on the relative volume error.
Both criteria pass on the shortcut-off build and on the candidate, and both still
fail a deliberately broken solve.
On the merged source the returned states repeat the earlier preservation maxima
exactly, ionic and sequential Khudaida evaluations fall, and MEA work is unchanged.
This is numerical verification on manufactured references and declared local cases;
delivered review has not run.

## Native check criteria at the rounding floor

The earlier affected check failed the action forward-bound comparison at two
manufactured bubble inputs and the wide-ionic reference's pressure closure.
[The diagnosis](results/equivalence/check-failure-diagnosis.json) traced both to
criteria that omit a rounding term the shortcut's state change reshuffles.

**Action forward bound.** The identical-species bubble has an exact response
$z^*$ in the equilibrated chart. The computed Jacobian $\tilde J$ carries its own
evaluation error $\Delta J$: the dense-liquid chemical-potential rows' composition
entries differ from their exact value $\pm\tfrac12$ through cancellation against
the liquid log-volume column. Then $z^*$ solves a perturbed computed system with
normwise backward error

$$
\eta_J=\frac{\lVert R\,\Delta J\,z^*\rVert_\infty}
{\lVert R\tilde JC\rVert_\infty\lVert C^{-1}z^*\rVert+\lVert R\tilde Jz^*\rVert_\infty},
$$

in the same certified norm as the solve's own backward error $\eta$, so the
first-order forward error obeys

$$
\frac{\lVert C^{-1}(\hat z-z^*)\rVert}{\lVert C^{-1}z^*\rVert}\le
2\kappa_\infty(\eta+\eta_J)+\epsilon .
$$

Each backward error enters with the factor $2\kappa_\infty$ because it perturbs
both matrix and right-hand side; $\epsilon$ covers the final rounding of each
returned observable. The check computes $\Delta J$ from the Jacobian the action
factors: on every rung the action's matrix equals the compiled Jacobian bit for bit.
The former bound omitted $\eta_J$, so it failed whenever refinement drove $\eta$
below the Jacobian's own error.

**Wide-ionic volume closure.** The binary128 reference uses the volume $v$.
Its pressure limit was the evaluation noise floor, which the converged Newton
iterate straddled. The final check is now the volume forward error
$|P(v)-P|\le 2^{-100}|\partial P/\partial v|\,v$, to first order
$|\delta v/v|\le 2^{-100}$, which moves the reference values far below their
Richardson targets. The Newton loop is unchanged.

{{< include results/merged-main/tables.md >}}

Both defect probes were disposable builds. An action solved in the raw,
unequilibrated system is refused as ill-conditioned at the four highest-condition
rungs that its bound cannot admit. Truncating the volume Newton before or after
one step leaves the closure ratio many orders above one at the first reference call.
[Criterion records](results/merged-main/criteria.json) retain every rung, every
closure distribution and both probes, and
[qualification provenance](results/merged-main/qualification.json) identifies the
merged source and wheels.
The bound is first-order and valid while $\Delta J$ stays at rounding level; the
Jacobian's own correctness is owned by the exact-derivative checks, not by this
bound.

## Question, method and basis

Can the shared driver's fresh Newton correction avoid damped trials at the
rounding floor without losing the physical state of unchanged polishing?
[Issue 272](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/272) owns the accepted
amendment and preservation budgets. [ALG-EQUILIBRIUM](../../engine/docs/science/algorithms.md#alg-equilibrium)
owns the complete stopping rule, including consistent infinity norms, full-rank
factorizations, the forward estimate, the current-best guard and positive free
amounts. Thermodynamic definitions remain
[material balance](../../engine/docs/equations.md#material_balance) and
[chemical-potential stationarity](../../engine/docs/equations.md#chemical_potential_stationarity).
No equation-of-state formulation, row criterion or solver tolerance changes.

The local correction tolerance is read from the installed candidate's numerical
policy. Log compositions and log packing fractions keep their chart scales.
Each positive free phase amount uses its own amount in mol; free temperature
and pressure use their current K and Pa values; multipliers remain absolute in
RT units. A nonpositive free amount disables the shortcut. The current correction
must be fresh: a preceding small direction does not bound the next one.

The observable-relative budget applies to temperature, pressure and each phase
density. Species with fed amounts below one millionth of total feed use their
own phase-species amount as the trace-relative denominator. This conservative
screen also includes unfed reacting products. Other species amounts and each
phase total use the reference phase total as their phase-relative denominator.
Both-zero amounts agree exactly. Ordered phase identities and identical input
declarations are retained.

Each budget is ten times the local correction tolerance. The shortcut omits only
a correction bounded by that tolerance in the same scaled coordinates. On these
qualified inputs, unchanged polishing then applies at most rounding-level
corrections. An excess is a finding for diagnosis; it does not authorize a wider
tolerance. This local estimate is not a general state-error certificate:
composition normalization, density conversion, condition estimation and later
Newton directions limit that interpretation.

## Historical qualification and damped-trial diagnosis

The earlier damped-trial predicates did not separate wasted ionic and Khudaida
trials from required productive steps.
The historical correction-size comparison failed four checks under the former
criteria.
These records remain below with their original values and inspected snapshots;
the owner subsequently required the equivalence requalification above.

## Damped-trial diagnosis on unchanged polishing

The diagnostic wheel uses unchanged polishing from main; its exact revision and
wheel identities are in [provenance](results/damped-stop/provenance.json).
The recording-only wheel changes no equation, Newton direction, damping fraction,
row criterion or best-point selection. Returned values and comparison checks are
compared exactly against the pristine wheel before interpreting the trace.

For current chart coordinates $x$, rounded trial coordinates $x_\alpha$,
raw rows $r$, and the exact current Jacobian $J$, the native recorder computes

$$
\widehat r_\alpha=r+J(x_\alpha-x),\qquad
\widehat{\Delta m}=\lVert r\rVert_\infty-\lVert\widehat r_\alpha\rVert_\infty.
$$

The accumulation uses extended precision and the actual representable trial
coordinates. It therefore includes addition rounding in the proposed displacement.
The assembly estimate is $f_j=u\sum_k|t_{jk}|$, with $u$ the binary64 unit roundoff
and $t_{jk}$ the terms of raw row $j$ in
[the shared row assembly](../../engine/native/equilibrium/request_compile.cpp).
This estimates final assembly rounding. It does not bound error within the
equation-of-state derivatives, source completion or coordinate transformations.
The recorder retains the native association-gradient estimate separately; its
maximum is the native evaluation’s reported floor. Taking the larger estimate
also rejects productive corrections and cannot certify a no-progress decision.

Ulps mean distances between ordered binary64 representations. The coordinate
files retain every current value, undamped correction, rounded trial and distance.
The complete [trial table](results/damped-stop/trials.md),
[row table](results/damped-stop/rows.csv) and
[coordinate table](results/damped-stop/coordinates.csv) retain every evaluated
trial, including all sequential Khudaida points and the native parameter-fit calls.
A productive trial means it satisfies main’s existing raw-contraction and
physical-composition admission, not that it establishes physical validation.

{{< include ../../build/notebook-data/polish-damped.md >}}

All rejected ionic and sequential Khudaida trials remain physically inside the
composition cutoff. Their recomputed chemical rows fail strict raw contraction;
none is rejected by the extension-ratio rule. These trials change representable
coordinates, rather than repeat the current point. The linear prediction remains
a descent on every such trial, but recomputing the thermodynamic rows reverses it.
Extended-precision summation of already evaluated row operands still rejects
every one of these trials. It also changes the verdict on an accepted ionic
quarter trial, so changing summation precision would change the governing method.
These observations locate the discrepancy beyond a duplicate-coordinate test or
final assembly rounding alone; they do not isolate one electrolyte or association
operation as its cause.

The norm-wide estimate catches an accepted ionic quarter trial, productive fit
trials, an isomerization correction and a productive masking correction.
Comparing each row with its own rounding estimate avoids the masking correction,
but still catches productive fit and isomerization steps and saves no ionic or
Khudaida work. Comparing only the currently controlling merit row catches fewer
rejected ionic trials and still catches productive fit steps. Exact-coordinate,
previous-trial identity and nonpositive-prediction checks identify no rejected
ionic or Khudaida trial. A stop after a rejected full trial also cannot meet the
ionic evaluation limit while retaining its productive quarter trial.

The historical damped-trial design outcome was **optimization not adopted**. No runtime rule,
new numerical-policy value, tolerance change or caller-specific selection is
proposed. This finite replay falsifies the tested predicates; it is not a proof
that every possible pre-evaluation predicate is impossible. Main’s work remains
the expected work. The preservation budgets, physical masking and small-phase
cases, extensive stationarity and solved-state derivative criteria remain required
for any different proposal. Independent design review and issue disposition stay
with the accountable lead; these results have not been promoted for manuscript use.

## Falsifiers and physical meaning

The masking input uses three identical ethane species in one vapor phase with
the source test's trace-feed reacting isomerization declaration. The candidate
never takes the shortcut on this case and preserves both reacting species amounts
exactly. The historical norm-band counterexample remains in
[original state rows](results/physical-state-comparison.csv),
[row operands](results/operands.csv) and [Newton directions](results/steps.csv).
The small raw residual did not justify omitting its trace correction.

The free-temperature declaration comes from `test_cold_vapor.py`; the
free-pressure declaration comes from `test_continuation.py`. Both retain their
states within the approved budgets and take the fresh-correction shortcut.
The [small positive vapor declaration](results/amendment-2/small-phase-input.json)
lies above the topology cutoff. Its phase-relative correction exceeds the local
threshold while the same amount correction relative to feed is below it.
A bounded native solve of the installed Engine Jacobian confirms that changing
only the free-amount scale to feed admits the complete forward bound.
[amount-scaling.csv](results/resumed/amount-scaling.csv) retains both full-coordinate
norms, the alternative forward bound and factorization ranks. The candidate
blocks the shortcut and keeps unchanged-polish work and states.
Unloaded MEA retains its fourth accepted trial.

The bounded native diagonal-system falsifier retains a tiny backward residual
with an analytically known larger forward correction. Its manufactured input
is in [qualification.json](results/resumed/qualification.json); its computed
bound and reference are in
[admission-falsifier.csv](results/resumed/admission-falsifier.csv).
The same check rejects a singular factorization and admits a resolved small
correction. The paused test's reporting fields were corrected while preserving
its numerical expectation and tolerance.

## Historical failed checks and correction admission

[gate-findings.csv](results/resumed/gate-findings.csv) retains the failed
candidate comparisons and their unchanged limits. Both affected and full checks
find the same failures. These comprise two solved-state action transport
comparisons, the extensive KKT stationarity identity and a near-zero parameter regression
variance comparison. Replaying those four tests against the identified
merged-main wheel passes all four.

The bounded KKT replay reuses the exact identical-ethane isomerization test
at its stated temperature, pressure, equilibrium constant and feed amount.
Its analytic composition and first-through-third thermal-action checks pass,
while extensive-objective stationarity fails. Native detailed capture shows
full rank, a current-best point, positive amount, and a forward bound below the
local correction threshold when the candidate stops. Unchanged polishing
continues and satisfies the identity. This reproduced case shows that the
accepted coordinate bound does not preserve every unchanged numerical check;
it does not identify a new admissible stopping criterion.

The [candidate numerical rows](results/resumed/candidate-kkt-values.csv),
[baseline numerical rows](results/resumed/baseline-kkt-values.csv),
[candidate polish trace](results/resumed/candidate-kkt-trace.csv) and
[baseline polish trace](results/resumed/baseline-kkt-trace.csv) retain the cause.
At that stage, the local correction bound did not preserve the former check
criteria. The owner subsequently adopted the equivalence standard; the fresh
qualification above changes the test criteria under that authority while
retaining the runtime correction predicate.

## Paired timing and uncertainty

`tools/time-key-solves` installs the two identified wheels, uses identical
physical inputs and a common accepted start where applicable, and pins both
workers to the same CPU with one numerical thread. Every counterbalanced pair
includes AB and BA blocks. Imports and input preparation lie outside the solve
clock. Pair changes average the two block percentage changes. Median absolute
deviation and the observed range describe shared-host variability; they are
not confidence intervals. Deterministic work counts are the speed gate.

These are scalar work, error-budget and elapsed-time comparisons on fixed
inputs. Tables identify the controlling case and retain timing spread directly;
a plot would add no continuous physical relationship or accuracy information.

## Reference refresh (#754)

The [accepted diagnosis](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/754#issuecomment-6328215094)
attributes the MEA shift to [#353](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/353)'s
intended infinite-dilution reference correction and brackets the masking shift at
[#633](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/633)'s trace-inventory correction.
The MEA attribution is supported by the source change and numerical probes. It
cannot be isolated with published wheels: the earliest available wheel already
contains the shift. The diagnosis path and full SHA-256 are retained in the
[qualification record](results/issue-754/qualification.json).

The [original reference rows](results/amendment-2/baseline-states.csv) remain frozen,
with their original reference source and wheel identified in the leaf README and
[historical wheel record](results/resumed/baseline-wheel.json). The declarations
remain byte-identical. The fresh reference and independent repeat use one wheel
built from the current main producer, with every solve and comparison operation
unchanged. Both freshly serialized state tables and traces reproduce the #720
numerical owners byte for byte; their records point to those single owners.
This comparison checks repetition on the accepted equations. The earlier
shortcut-disabled comparisons retain their original scope and producer identities.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

fresh = Path('results/issue-754')
qualification = json.loads((fresh / 'qualification.json').read_text())
reference = json.loads((fresh / 'baseline-wheel.json').read_text())
root = Path('../..')
before = list(csv.DictReader((root / qualification['historical_maxima_path']).open()))
after = list(csv.DictReader((fresh / 'budget-maxima.csv').open()))
residuals = list(csv.DictReader((fresh / 'residual-maxima.csv').open()))
limit = qualification['comparison_limit']
print(f"Producer commit: `{qualification['producer_commit']}`.\n")
print(f"Installed wheel SHA-256: `{reference['sha256']}`.\n")
print(f"Both runs solve **{qualification['solved_states']} of {len(residuals)} states**, "
      f"with **{qualification['requested_tolerances_met']} of {len(residuals)} requested tolerances met**.\n")
print(f"The **{limit:.0e} comparison limit is unchanged**.\n")
print('| Comparison basis | Historical reference difference | Refreshed reference difference | Unchanged limit |')
print('|---|---:|---:|---:|')
for old, new in zip(before, after, strict=True):
    assert old['budget'] == new['budget']
    print(f"| {old['budget']} | {float(old['difference']):.15g} | {float(new['difference']):.15g} | {limit:.0e} |")
print('\nTemperature is in K, pressure in Pa, phase/species amounts in mol, and all comparison differences are dimensionless.\n')
print('| State | Maximum absolute classified residual | Requested row tolerance | Met |')
print('|---|---:|---:|---|')
for row in residuals:
    print(f"| {row['case']} | {float(row['maximum_classified_residual']):.8g} | {float(row['row_tolerance']):.0e} | {row['requested_tolerance_met']} |")
small = next(r for r in csv.DictReader((root / qualification['historical_comparison_path']).open())
             if r['case'] == 'small-positive-phase' and r['quantity'] == 'phase_amount' and r['index'] == '1')
absolute = abs(float(small['candidate']) - float(small['baseline']))
print(f"\nThe small vapor amount is {float(small['candidate']):.8g} mol. Its historical "
      f"difference is only {absolute:.8g} mol absolute, despite a "
      f"{float(small['difference']):.8g} phase-relative difference.\n")
```

The small-phase case is a rounding-amplification note, not a loosened bound.
Recovering a tiny phase from differences of order-one inventories amplifies
binary64 rounding. The current s1/s2 amounts in the masking case satisfy the
analytic inventory and its one-to-three split to rounding, as the diagnosis
establishes. The comparison limit and every requested row tolerance are retained.
The original comparison also passes its trace, correction and work assertions.

These are three scalar preservation maxima and per-state residual checks; a plot
would add no physical relationship. The result supports a reference refresh on
accepted current equations and local numerical verification on these declared
cases. It supplies no physical validation, global stability result, rigorous
forward-error bound, or isolated pre-/post-#353 comparison. Independent delivered
review and investigator promotion remain separate.
